titulo: Search Console and Bing Webmaster: verify your site
lead: The two free dashboards are the only official source for what Google and Bing see on your site: what is indexed, which searches show you, and, since 2026, what appears in the AI features. Before you create a new account, check whether someone has already verified the site. It happens more often than you'd think.
objetivo: check whether the site is already verified, then verify it in Search Console and Bing Webmaster, with the sitemap submitted in both.

aprende.t: Check in DNS whether the site is already verified
Create the domain property in Search Console
Connect Bing Webmaster by importing from Search Console
Know what the AI dashboards show in 2026

hero_alt: A woman in a small office checks charts on a computer screen, with a notebook beside her.

nos.detalhe: A google-site-verification TXT record in DNS shows that someone has already verified the site in Search Console. Ask who has access before you create another account.
In Search Console, the domain property is verified with a TXT record in DNS and covers www, non-www, and subdomains all at once. It's the method's recommended way.
Once Search Console is ready, Bing Webmaster imports the site from there, with no other DNS record. Bing feeds Copilot, and IndexNow tells Bing about every new publication (lesson 8).
Submit the sitemap address in both dashboards and check the status. A sitemap that's "pending" or shows an error is the first sign of a problem.

The Search Console generative AI report has applied to all sites since 08/31/2026 and shows impressions only. Bing's AI Performance (February 2026) and the Topics Portfolio (10/13/2026) are the only dashboards with official citations.

secoes.legenda: All free. Paid tools don't have data from Google's index: only estimates.

texto: Run the dig command on your domain. If google-site-verification shows up, someone has already verified it: find that account and ask for access.
A duplicate account splits the history and confuses whoever looks after the site.

exemplo.texto: One plan said "no Search Console" because it only looked in the code. The DNS showed the verification. The rule became: check the TXT record before claiming it doesn't exist.

texto: In Search Console, choose "Domain" and paste the TXT record it shows into your DNS panel (at the registrar or the CDN).
Propagation can take a few minutes; then click verify.

exemplo.texto: One property covers www, non-www, and subdomains like news. or eventos.

texto: At bing.com/webmasters, sign in with an account and choose to import from Google Search Console.
If you prefer, Bing also accepts its own verification. IndexNow notifies Bing even when the site isn't in this dashboard.
Submit the sitemap in both and note the date. The performance reports start filling up in a few days.
The following week, look at the page list and the sitemap status.

blocos.conteudo:
dig TXT seusite.com +short
# look for a line with google-site-verification=

Type:  TXT
Name:  @   (the root domain)
Value: google-site-verification=<code that Search Console shows>

Search Console: domain property <seusite.com>, verified on <mm/dd/yyyy>, account <who owns it>
Bing Webmaster: imported from Search Console on <mm/dd/yyyy>
Sitemap submitted: <https://www.seusite.com/sitemap.xml> — status <success / pending>

abas.html:
"google-site-verification=AbCdEf123exemplo"
"v=spf1 include:_spf.exemplo.com ~all"

The first line says the site already has an owner in Search Console. The second one is for email and has nothing to do with SEO.

• Prefix instead of domain: verifies only one version of the address and hides the rest.
  • Deleting the TXT record after verifying: Search Console asks for verification again.
  • Trusting a paid tool to know what's indexed: only the official dashboards have that data.

secoes.titulo: Practice: both dashboards up and running

exercicios.texto: Run dig TXT on your domain and note the result. If there is already a verification, find out whose account it is.
exercicios.pronto: you can tell whether the site was already verified and who has access.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Verified and with a sitemap
exercicios.texto: Create (or recover) the domain property in Search Console, import it into Bing Webmaster, and submit the sitemap in both.
exercicios.pronto: both dashboards show the site as verified and the sitemap with a status of success or pending, noted with the date.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: Before creating a Search Console account, what should you check?
opcoes: Whether the DNS already has a google-site-verification TXT record.
perguntas.explica: A TXT record in the DNS shows that someone has already verified the site. At INEMA, a plan claimed "no Search Console" by looking only at the code; the DNS said the opposite.

perguntas.p: Why is the domain property the right choice of method?
opcoes: It covers www, non-www, and subdomains in a single property.
perguntas.explica: With a prefix property, you verify only one version of the address. The domain property brings everything together and avoids separate histories.

perguntas.p: What does the generative AI report in Search Console show?
opcoes: Clicks and position in AI answers.
The text the AI wrote about you.
perguntas.explica: Since 08/31/2026, it applies to all sites and shows impressions. Official citations, for now, are only in Bing's AI Performance.

perguntas.p: A paid tool says 500 of your pages are on Google. Which should you trust?
perguntas.explica: Google says no third-party tool has access to its systems. The indexing data is in Search Console.

itens.texto: dig TXT: the site may already have an owner in Search Console.
A domain property covers all versions; Bing imports from it.
Search Console shows impressions in AI; Bing is the only one with official citations.
